summary: Charles Gabriel Seligman worked in history, archaeology, and other fields, studying medicine at St Thomas' Hospital Medical School (~1891–1896). He held the chair of Ethnology at the University of London and the London School of Economics from 1913 to 1934.

Charles Goodman specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Allan Gibbard by 2002 and served as an associate professor at Binghamton University (attested 2013).

A scholar of religious studies, Charles H. Long studied at Dunbar Junior College and the University of Chicago (BD, PhD). He served at Chicago (~1956–1974), UNC Chapel Hill and Duke (~1974–1987), Syracuse (~1987–1990), and UC Santa Barbara (~1990–1996).

Charles Hallisey is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1988). He held positions at Loyola University Chicago (~1987–1991), Harvard University (1996–2001, 2007), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (2001, 2005).

Indologist Charles Henry Tawney studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, where he was a fellow and tutor in 1860. He served at Presidency University (1866–1872; 1875–1892), Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1880), and as Librarian for the India Office (1892/1893–1903).

Charles Li works in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields. He held posts as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of British Columbia (attested 2020), at the CNRS (attested 2023), and at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Indologist and religious studies scholar Charles Malamoud studied at the University of Paris. He taught at the University of Lyon (~1968–1972) and served as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1978–1998).
Historian and archaeologist Charles Oman studied at New College, Oxford (~1878–1882). He held an academic post at the University of Oxford from around 1883 until 1946.

Charles Otto Blagden, active in linguistics, history, and archaeology, was educated at Dulwich College and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1882–1886). He later held a post at SOAS University of London from around 1917 to 1935.

Indologist and linguist Charles Philip Brown studied at East India Company College and with traditional teachers. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1817–1855) and became Professor of Telugu at the University of London (~1865–1884).

Charles Ramble works in Tibetology and religious studies, having studied at Durham and Oxford (DPhil 1981) under Michael Aris. He held positions at Oxford (2002–2005) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 2009).

Linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar Charles Rieu studied at Geneva and Bonn under Freytag, Gildemeister, and Lassen. He served at the British Museum from 1847 and as Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.

Charles Rockwell Lanman worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Yale and in Germany under Whitney, Weber, and Roth. He served at Johns Hopkins (~1876–1880) and held a professorship at Harvard University from 1880 to 1926.

Charles S. Prebish, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, studied under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. He held positions at Pennsylvania State University (~1972–2007) and the Numata Chair of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary.

Charles Taliaferro specializes in philosophy and religious studies. He was educated at Goddard College, the University of Rhode Island, Harvard Divinity School, and Brown University, and served as a professor at St. Olaf College from around 1985.

Philosopher Charles Taylor studied at McGill University (~1948–1952) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1952–1961). He held academic posts at Université de Montréal (~1961–1971), McGill University (~1961–1998), and Northwestern University (~2002).

Charles Wei-hsun Fu worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at National Taiwan University (~1952–1960) and the University of Illinois (~1966–1969), and held a post at Ohio University (~1969–1972).

Indologist and linguist Charles Wilkins studied under Kālinātha (~1778–1786). In addition to founding the Asiatic Society, he served as librarian for the East India Company and the India Office Library from around 1801 to 1836.
Charles Willemen works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied under William Reynolds Beal Acker and held a post as professor at Ghent University (attested 1999–2001).

Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin, working in Iranian/Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Indology, earned a law doctorate at the University of Liège (~1851–1855). He served as director of Collège Saint-Quirin and professor at KU Leuven (~1871–1899).
